1. Leave granted.
 2. The appellant was travelling in an auto-rickshaw and when it  reached near railway bridge, the driver lost control and dashed  against a tree as a result of which the appellant received multiple  injuries.
His left leg was eventually amputed below knee and his
right leg was amputed above knee.
The appellant was 42 year  at that time.
He filed a Claim Petition before the Motor Accident  Claims Tribunal No.VII, Bijapur, Karnataka (for   Tribunal) under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text:
Petition filed by the appellant, the High Court, vide order dated Reason:
 04.03.2020, granted a revised compensation of Rs.9,13,344/- to him.
2 3. Still aggrieved, the appellant is before us by way  present appeal.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. The admitted facts are that the appellant is an agriculturist and has lost both the legs i.e. left leg below knee and right leg above knee.
The appellant, thus, cannot carry out the agricultural vocation and is fully dependant upon skilled or manual labour for the agricultural activities.
The appellant whose family is fully dependant on him, claimed that his monthly income was Rs.6,000/-.
The High Court has assessed the monthly income of the appellant at Rs.3250/-, which, in our considered opinion, is quite on lower side.
It is difficult to accept that with such a meagre inco appellant would have been maintaining his family.

In the absenc any contrary evidence, we are inclined to accept that the monthly income of the appellant was not less than Rs.5,000/-. 
accordingly.

6. Having assessed the monthly income of the appella Rs.5,000/-, coupled with the fact that he has admittedly suffered Siddappa vs The Branch Manager Oriental Insurance ... on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68886782/
2 100% disability, the appellant is held entitled to  compensation towards loss of income and future prospects besides medical expenses and other losses, as tabulated by the High Court.

8. The appeal stands allowed to the extent indicated above.
